_comment: The Android wrapper, after Play Games made the TWA impossible.
A TWA is a real Chrome tab shown inside an app, and by design there is no
bridge between its JavaScript and any Android code ג€” which is exactly what
makes it a browser rather than a WebView, and exactly why the page can
never call Play Games. See docs/PLAY-GAMES.md.
Everything here that is not about the wrapper is deliberately the SAME as
android/twa-manifest.json: the package id, the key, the name, the colours.
The next version has to be an update to the app that is already in closed
testing, not a new listing ג€” the testers, the clock and the rating all hang
versionCode 3 because 2 is the TWA already uploaded.
4 is the first build with the Amanda launcher icon on it ג€” 3 went to Play
5 fixes two things 4 got wrong. The full-screen flags were written onto
AppTheme.NoActionBar, and the manifest gives MainActivity
AppTheme.NoActionBarLaunch ג€” so they were set on a style nothing uses and
the status bar stayed across the top of the game. And the way back from a
Google sign-in is a custom scheme now, because Chrome would not hand the
https link to the app mid-redirect.
_url: The WebView loads the live site, which is what the TWA does today.
Or chose this over bundling the build into the app, and the deciding fact
is that a code change reaches a phone in a minute instead of waiting for a
Play release. His own day-to-day change ג€” the words ג€” reaches players
without a release EITHER way, because the game fetches copy, cards and
live content from the server at runtime.
Two things were checked before choosing it. The server answers with
`access-control-allow-origin: *`, so a WebView origin is not refused; and
the service worker registers normally inside a WebView, so the game still
opens without a connection after the first run.
_games: The number Play Console issues when the game is linked to Play Games
Services. It goes into AndroidManifest.xml as
com.google.android.gms.games.APP_ID, and the app CRASHES ON LAUNCH without
it ג€” not a warning, a crash, which is worth knowing before a tester sees
it. Leave it empty and the prepare script refuses to build rather than
Play Console -> Grow users -> Play Games services -> Setup and management
_signing: The same upload key as the TWA. A different key would be a different app
to Google however much the package id matches.
_orientation: What the TWA did and the WebView stopped doing.
Or: *"before version two everything already worked. Now it suddenly goes
to the browser to sign in, and when the phone is not landscape it tells me
to rotate it instead of just showing the game landscape."* Both are the
same kind of regression: things a TWA got for free that a WebView has to
android/twa-manifest.json says orientation: landscape, and bubblewrap
turned that into a locked activity. The game could not BE in portrait, so
the rotate-hint screen was unreachable. Capacitor generates no
screenOrientation at all, so the activity follows the phone, the game is
drawn in portrait, and the hint is what the player sees.
A web manifest does not help here: the WebView is a native activity and
sensorLandscape rather than the TWA's plain landscape: both ways up work,
so a child holding the phone the other way round is not shown an upside
down game. Neither one can ever reach portrait.
